title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of N-(2-amino-phenyl)-5-(4-aryl- pyrimidin-2-yl) amino)-1H-indole-2-carboxamide derivatives as novel inhibitors of CDK9 and class I HDACs for cancer treatment.
authors: Chen, Xiaohui; Li, Rongna; Qiu, Yingkun; Lin, Fanhong; Chen, Shutong; Li, Xiaodan; Sun, Hui; Jiang, Guanmin; Fang, Hua; Qin, Jingbo; Fang, Meijuan
one_liner_zh: 该文为CDK9/HDAC小分子抑制剂的设计合成与抗癌活性评价，涉及蛋白-小分子对接，但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The mechanisms underlying transcriptional dysregulation in tumorigenesis have received considerable attention as promising therapeutic targets to combat human cancer. Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9) and class I histone deacetylases (HDACs) are significant therapeutic targets due to their pivotal roles in the dysregulated transcriptional programs characteristic of many cancers. Furthermore, the combinatorial transcriptional therapy with CDK9 and class I HDAC inhibitors has been shown to have a synergistic anticancer effect. In this study, a series of novel N-(2-amino-phenyl)-5-(4-aryl-pyrimidin-2-yl) amino)-1H-indole-2-carboxamide derivatives were designed and synthesized as novel dual-functional inhibitors targeting CDK9 and HDAC signaling pathways for cancer treatment. Among the synthesized compounds, 13ea demonstrated potent anti-proliferative activities (IC(50) < 5.0 muM) in various cancer cell lines (HeLa, MDA-MB-231, HepG2). In addition, 13ea was found to significantly inhibit the phosphorylation function of CDK9 and the deacetylation function of class I HDACs. Furthermore, 13ea was found to inhibit the protein activity of CDK9 (IC(50) = 0.17 muM), HDAC1 (IC(50) = 1.73 muM), and HDAC3 (IC(50) = 1.11 muM). The docking studies predicted the binding patterns of 13ea in the active pockets of CDK9 and HDAC1/3. The cellular assays revealed that 13ea induced mitochondria-related apoptosis and G2/M phase arrest in cancer cells, showing superior activities compared to those of AZD-5438 (a CDK9 inhibitor) and Mocetinostat (an inhibitor of class I HDACs). Notably, the in vivo assay demonstrated that 13ea (30 mg/kg) exhibited significant inhibition on MDA-MB-231 xenograft tumor growth, with a tumor shrinkage rate of 76.83 %. In summary, we have identified 13ea as a novel CDK9/HDAC inhibitor with excellent anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤发生中转录失调的机制作为对抗人类癌症的有前景治疗靶点，已受到广泛关注。细胞周期蛋白依赖性激酶9（CDK9）和I类组蛋白去乙酰化酶（HDACs）因其在多种癌症特征性失调转录程序中的关键作用，成为重要的治疗靶点。此外，CDK9与I类HDAC抑制剂联合的转录治疗已被证明具有协同抗癌效果。在本研究中，设计并合成了一系列新型N-(2-氨基苯基)-5-(4-芳基嘧啶-2-基)氨基)-1H-吲哚-2-甲酰胺衍生物，作为靶向CDK9和HDAC信号通路的新型双功能抑制剂，用于癌症治疗。在合成的化合物中，13ea在多种癌细胞系（HeLa、MDA-MB-231、HepG2）中表现出强效抗增殖活性（IC(50) < 5.0 μM）。此外，发现13ea显著抑制CDK9的磷酸化功能和I类HDACs的去乙酰化功能。进一步地，13ea被证明抑制CDK9（IC(50) = 0.17 μM）、HDAC1（IC(50) = 1.73 μM）和HDAC3（IC(50) = 1.11 μM）的蛋白活性。对接研究预测了13ea在CDK9和HDAC1/3活性口袋中的结合模式。细胞实验揭示，13ea在癌细胞中诱导线粒体相关凋亡和G2/M期阻滞，显示出优于AZD-5438（一种CDK9抑制剂）和Mocetinostat（一种I类HDAC抑制剂）的活性。值得注意的是，体内实验表明，13ea（30 mg/kg）对MDA-MB-231异种移植肿瘤生长表现出显著抑制，肿瘤缩小率为76.83%。总之，我们鉴定出13ea作为一种新型CDK9/HDAC抑制剂，在体外和体内均具有优异的抗癌活性。
